answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because horizon only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
